references.text: Prohibition against oppressing one's neighbor or robbing him, including withholding a worker's wages until the next day
Prohibition against oppressing or mistreating foreigners, with a reminder that the Israelites themselves were foreigners in Egypt
Exhortation not to despise one's neighbor but to show mercy to the poor
The prophet's accusation against those who oppress day laborers by withholding wages, along with widows, fatherless children, and foreigners
Warning that the withheld wages of workers cry out, and their cry has reached the ears of the Lord of Hosts
Continuation of the command specifying that wages must be paid on the same day, before sunset
Command to support those who become poor and lose their livelihood, whether they are brothers or foreigners
